info.title: z/OS Data Gatherer: SMF Data REST Services
info.description:
z/OS Data Gatherer REST Services 


The SMF records must be sorted by following SMF header fields: SMFHDR_Date (SMF date), SMFHDR_Time (SMF time) and SMFHDR_SID (SMF System identification)
 


 To reduce both, network and client workload, any field or structure with the value 'null' or empty are not included in the response. This means that a field or structure with one of these values can be present in a Schema but not found in the Response.

Two Vendor Extensions Groups are used in this OpenApi Specification: 
  - x-zdg: 	 extensions that are specific for z/OS Data Gatherer or that have different meaning in other IBM z/OS products 
 - x-zml: 	 extensions that may be found in other IBM z/OS products or described using Z-Markup Language with the same meaning 

The following vendor extensions are used: 
  - x-zdg-interpreted-value: 	 denotes that the value provided by the z/OS Data Gatherer is post-processed 
  - x-zdg-is-artificial: 	 denotes that the element is artificially created and does not correspond to any field from the original macro/structure 
  - x-zdg-key-composition: 	 describes the uniquely identifiable key of the structure (as child) if used in a parent-child relationship (e.g., as one specific entry of same type). The key is one or more structure fields or 'Indexed', which means the sequential creation count 
  - x-zdg-max-size: 	 maximal length of the structure (in bytes) at the highest release 
  - x-build-timestamp: 	 the application build timestamp 
  - x-modules-version: 	 the application modules version 
  - x-zml-bit-offset: 	 the bit-index of the element (used for sub-byte fields only) 
  - x-zml-bit-size: 	 the bit-length of the element (used for sub-byte fields only, or for elements which value starts at specific bit of the containing structure) 
  - x-zml-datatype: 	 the datatype of the field in the original mapping macro 
  - x-zml-offset: 	 the byte-offset at the original structure 
  - x-zml-size: 	 the byte-length of the element 
  - x-zml-structure-name: 	 the original name of the macro or structure that is described with the OpenApi compliant Schema 
  - x-zml-version: 	 the z/OS version under which the macro was compiled to get the following OpenApi compliant Schema 
  - x-zdg-is-meta: 	 when requesting data, these fields are included in 2 cases either showMeta=true is used, or meta-field is explicitly requested

get.description: Provides the cumulative information about each (sub-)type present in the SMF data source. If the SMF resource is accessed for the first time, or if the cache-validation failed, the result is cached and used every next time the discovery data is needed. Cache is stored for the time specified by the application settings

SMF113STY.description: Record subtype: 1 = Delta event counters 2 = Hardware event counters

SMF113_1_CSTYPE.description: Counter set type for counters recorded: 1 = Basic, 2 = Problem state, 3 = Crypto-activity, 4 = Extended 5 = z/OS 6 = MT-diagnostic

SMF113_1_CSUSELCDS.description: When on the counter set's counter data section described by fields SMF113_1_CDOF, SMF113_1_CDLN, and SMF113_1_CDON is mapped by SMF113_1_LCDS, otherwise it is mapped by SMF113_1_SCDS.

SMF113_1_CDOF.description: Offset to counter data section for this counter set, from the beginning of record. This can be to a SMF113_1_SCDS section or a SMF113_1_LCDS section, depending SMF113_1_CSUseLCDS

SMF113_1_CTS.description: Time when HIS Data collection started

SMF113_1_CTM.description: Time when this SMF record is written

SMF113_1_CPUID.description: Processor ID for which the hardware event counters are recorded. Note that zero is a valid processor number.

SMF113_1_CPUPROCCLASS.description: The processor type for which the hardware event counters are recorded. Will be one of the following: 0 = Standard CP 2 = zCBP or zAAP see SMF113_1_zCBP 4 = zIIP

SMF113_1_CPUSPEED.description: Processor speed for which the event counters are recorded. Speed is in cycles/microsecond.

SMF113_1_CTRVERSION0.description: Zero counter version number. This number is incremented when there is a change to the meaning of a counter in the z/OS counter set

SMF113_1_CTRVERSION1.description: First counter version number. This number is incremented when there is a change to the meaning of a counter or the number of installed counters in the Basic or Problem-state counter sets

SMF113_1_CTRVERSION2.description: Second counter version number. This number is incremented when there is a change to the meaning of a counter or the number of installed counters in the Crypto-activity, Extended or MT-diagnostic counters

SMF113_1_LOSTCTRDATA.description: When ON, the hardware indicated the hardware has lost counter data during the current interval

SMF113_1_LOSTMTDATA.description: When ON, the hardware indicated the hardware has lost MT counter data during the current interval

SMF113_1_ZCBP.description: When ON, a value of 2 for SMF113_1_CpuProcClass refers to a zCBP processor type, when off a zAAP processor type.

SMF113_1_CSOF.description: Offset to counter set section from beginning of record

SMF113_1_COREID.description: Core ID for which the hardware event counters are recorded. Note that zero is a valid core ID number.

SMF113_1_LCR.description: Event counter value delta. Contains the number of times a particular counter event has occurred since either the start of the HIS collection run, or the previous SMF 113 Type 1 record.

SMF113_SUBTYPE1_LONG_COUNTER_DATA_SECTIO.description: Long counter data section. This is used when the counter data delta is 8 bytes

SMF113SOF.description: Offset to subsystem section from beginning of record

SMF113IOF.description: Offset of identification section from beginning of record

SMF113DOF.description: Offset of data section from beginning of record

SMF113_1_SCR.description: Event counter value delta. Contains the number of times a particular counter event has occurred since either the start of the HIS collection run, or the previous SMF 113 Type 1 record.

SMF113_SUBTYPE1_SHORT_COUNTER_DATA_SECTI.description: Short counter data section. This is used when the counter data delta is 4 bytes

SMF113SSF.description: Bit 0 - Subsys ID after Sys ID

SMF113STY.description: Record subtype: 1 = Delta event counters 2 = Hardware event counters

SMF113_2_CR.description: Hardware event counter value. Contains the absolute number of times a particular hardware counter event has occurred.

SMF113_2_CST.description: Counterset type for counters recorded in SMF113_2_CR: 1 = Basic, 2 = Problem state, 3 = Crypto-activity, 4 = Extended

SMF113_2_CTS.description: Time when HIS Data collection started

SMF113_2_CTM.description: Time when this SMF record is written

SMF113_2_CPUPROCCLASS.description: The processor type for which the event counters are recorded. Will be one of the following: 0 = Standard CP 2 = zCBP or zAAP see SMF113_2_zCBP 4 = zIIP

SMF113_2_CFF.description: First SMF record for the instrumentation run. The counter values are the initial values.

SMF113_2_CFM.description: Middle SMF record (activated by interval timers). The counter values are intermediate values. The number of intermediate records varies from 0 to many, depending on the duration of the instrumentation run. An intermediate recrod is produced periodically based on the SMFINTVAL parameter.

SMF113_2_CFL.description: Final SMF record for the instrumentation run. The counter values are the values at the end of the run.

SMF113_2_CFNS.description: 1=Internal flag indicating SMF record is created on non-standard instrumentation hardware

SMF113_2_LOSTDATA.description: When ON, the hardware indicated the hardware has lost counter data on during the current interval

SMF113_2_ZCBP.description: When ON, a value of 2 for SMF113_2_CpuProcClass refers to a zCBP processor type, when off a zAAP processor type.

SMF113_2_CTRVN1.description: First counter version number. This number is incremented when there is a change to the meaning of a counter or the number of installed counters in the Basic or Problem-state counter sets

SMF113_2_CTRVN2.description: Second counter version number. This number is incremented when there is a change to the meaning of a counter or the number of installed counters in the Crypto-activity or Extended counter sets

SMF113_2_CSOF.description: Offset to counter set section from beginning of record

SMF113_2_CDOF.description: Offset to counter data section from beginning of record

SMF113_2_CDON.description: Number of counter data sections. This is the total number of SMF113_2_CDS sections for all the counter sets

SMF113_2_CPSP.description: Processor speed for which the event counters are recorded. Speed is in cycles/microsecond.

SMF113_2_CPUID.description: Processor ID for which the hardware event counters are recorded. Note that zero is a valid processor ID.

SMF113SOF.description: Offset to subsystem section from beginning of record

SMF113IOF.description: Offset of identification section from beginning of record

SMF113DOF.description: Offset of data section from beginning of record

SMF30ATR.description: Number of Requests Processed by this TP

SMF30DC.description: Number of conversations associated with the transaction program (TP) ID, both currently active and deallocated.

SMF30DSC.description: Number of times the transaction program (TP) issued Send call. Note: Due to the possibilty of an interval or ste ending in the middle of a SEND call, this field may contain zer while SMF30DDS contains a non-zero value.

SMF30DDS.description: Amount of data sent by the transaction program (TP).

SMF30DRC.description: Number of times the transaction program (TP) issued a Receive call. Note: Due to the possibilty of an interval or step ending in the middle of a RECEIVE call, this field may contain zero while SMF30DDR contains a non-zero value.

SMF30DDR.description: Amount of data received by the transaction program (TP).

SMF30DTR.description: Number of APPC/MVS transactions programs scheduled by the APPC/MVS transaction scheduler (ASCH).

SMF30RSN.description: The system name for the system on which the element was initially started or blank for the initial start. The current system name is in the SMF30SYN field.

SMF30RGT.description: Time (local) Element requested REGISTER Function, in hundredths of a second

SMF30RGD.description: Date Element requested REGISTER Function, in the form 0cyydddF (where 'F' is the sign)

SMF30RWT.description: Time (local) Element requested WAITPRED function, in hundredths of a second Note that this is the time that the function was requested, not satisfied. 0, if the element has not requested the function.

SMF30RWD.description: Date Element requested WAITPRED function, in the following format: 0cyydddF (where 'F' is the sign) 0, if the element has not requested the function.

SMF30RYT.description: Time (local) Element was READY, in hundredths of a second 0, if the element is not yet READY

SMF30RYD.description: Date Element was READY, in the following format: 0cyydddF (where 'F' is the sign) 0, if the element is not yet READY

SMF30RTT.description: Time (local) Element was DEREGISTERED, in hundredths of a second 0, if the element is not yet DEREGISTERED or ended abnormally.

SMF30RTD.description: Date Element was DEREGISTERED, in the following format: 0cyydddF (where 'F' is the sign) 0, if the element is not yet DEREGISTERED or ended abnormally.

SMF30SLC.description: JOB was cancelled by SMFLIM parmlib policy. Note that SMF30USI will also be on.

SMF30ERE.description: STEP ENDED DUE TO OpenMVS EXEC() FUNCTION REQUEST

SMF30CNR.description: Job was evicted via the $EJnn,STEP,HOLD or equivalent command. This bit is set for subtype 4 (step end) records only.

SMF30_CONTAINER_ID.description: Container ID, padded with blanks if needed

SMF30_CONTAINER_QUAL.description: Container Qualifier, padded with blanks if needed

SMF30_POD_ID.description: Pod ID, padded with blanks if needed

SMF30_INSTFLGS1.description: Instruction counter related flags. If a bit in this byte is on in the subtype 2/3 record, it will be on in the subtype 4 record. Likewise between subtype 4 and subtype 5 records.

SMF30_INSTCAPTDISRUPTION.description: There was a disruption in the collection of instruction counts or the counts could not be obtained

SMF30_INSTCAPTLIMITED.description: The following fields contain incomplete data: (SRM could not deliver deltas or values for this interval) SMF30_Inst_CP_Enclave SMF30_Inst_Offload_Enclave SMF30_Inst_OffloadOnCP_Enclave SMF30_Inst_CP_DepEnc SMF30_Inst_Offload_DepEnc SMF30_Inst_OffloadOnCP_DepEnc

SMF30_INST_CP_TASK.description: The number of instructions executed while running on a standard processor as a task when it is not eligible for an offload processor nor is it associated with an enclave.

SMF30_INST_CP_NONPREEMPTSRB.description: The number of instructions executed while running on a standard processor as a non-preemptable SRB.

SMF30_INST_CP_PREEMPTSRB.description: The number of instructions executed while running on a standard processor as a preemptable or client SRB when it is not associated with an enclave.

SMF30_INST_OFFLOAD.description: The number of instructions executed while running on an offload processor when not associated with an enclave.

SMF30_INST_OFFLOADONCP.description: The number of instructions executed while running on a standard processor as eligible for an offload processor when not associated with an enclave.

SMF30_INST_CP_ENCLAVE.description: The number of instructions executed while running on a standard processor as not eligible for an offload processor for an independent enclave.

SMF30_INST_OFFLOAD_ENCLAVE.description: The number of instructions executed while running on an offload processor for an independent enclave.

SMF30_INST_OFFLOADONCP_ENCLAVE.description: The number of instructions executed while running on a standard processor as eligible for an offload processor for an independent enclave.

SMF30_INST_CP_DEPENC.description: The number of instructions executed while running on a standard processor as not eligible for an offload processor for a dependent enclave.

SMF30_INST_OFFLOAD_DEPENC.description: The number of instructions executed while running on an offload processor for a dependent enclave.

SMF30_INST_OFFLOADONCP_DEPENC.description: The number of instructions executed while running on a standard processor as eligible for an offload processor for a dependent enclave.

SMF30_CRYPCTRS_ENTRY_ID.description: Crypto Counter entry identifier, The IFASMFCN macro contains equates and meanings for each entry ID. The equate names start with SMF_CrypCtrs.

SMF30_CRYPCTRS_COUNT.description: Crypto Counter value. This field contains the instruction counts used within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step, or job.

SMF30DDN.description: DD NAME FOR THIS DATA SET

SMF30BLK.description: NUMBER OF BLOCKS FOR THIS D.S.

SMF30CBS.description: Changed blocksize for the data set. Post processors should use this field to avoid the possibility of negative numbers.

SMF30UIF.description: User-defined identification field (taken from common exit parameter area, not from USER= parameter on job statement).

SMF30ISS.description: Interval Start Time for Subtype 2 and 3 records (STCK format)

SMF30IET.description: Interval End Time for Subtype 2, 3 and 6 Records (STCK format)

SMF30JCLID1.description: JES-computed binary identifier for the job that was submitted (using method 1), if provided by the primary subsystem

SMF30JCLID2.description: JES-computed binary identifier for the job that was submitted (using method 2), if provided by the primary subsystem

SMF30JOBTOKEN.description: Binary identifier for the job, if provided by the primary subsystem

SMF30HOLDUNTIL.description: A UTC timestamp represented by the first 6 bytes (bits 0-47) of an ETOD value. This is the resolved HOLDUNTL value for the job (from JCL or JES2 symbol on the internal reader interface), if provided by the primary subsystem

SMF30DEADLINE.description: A UTC timestamp represented by the first 6 bytes (bits 0-47) of an ETOD value. This is the resolved DEADLINE value for the job (from JES2 symbol on the internal reader interface), if provided by the primary subsystem

SMF30TEP.description: Total blocks transferred (Accumulated EXCP counts - valid up to 'FFFFFFFE'x, zero and invalid when SMF30TEF is set)

SMF30TCN.description: TOTAL DEVICE CONNECT TIME FOR THIS ADDRESS SPACE

SMF30MFL.description: DEVICE CONNECT TIME MAY BE INCORRECT

SMF30IIN.description: The following fields contain incomplete data: (SRM could not deliver deltas or values for this interval) SMF30AIC SMF30EIC SMF30AID SMF30EID SMF30AIW SMF30EIW SMF30AIS SMF30EIS

SMF30AIC.description: DASD I/O connect time for address space plus dependent enclaves in 128-microsecond units

SMF30AID.description: DASD I/O disconnect time for address space plus dependent enclaves in 128-microsecond units

SMF30AIW.description: DASD I/O pending plus control unit queue time for address space plus dependent enclaves in 128-microsecond units

SMF30AIS.description: DASD I/O start subchannel count for address space plus dependent enclaves

SMF30EIC.description: DASD I/O connect time for independent enclaves owned by the address space in 128-microsecond units

SMF30EID.description: DASD I/O disconnect time for independent enclaves owned by the address space in 128-microsecond units

SMF30EIW.description: DASD I/O pending plus control unit queue time for independent enclaves owned by the address space in 128-microsecond units

SMF30EIS.description: DASD I/O start subchannel count for independent enclaves owned by the address space

SMF30TEX.description: Total blocks transferred - Accumulated EXCP counts - This is the 8-byte equivalent of SMF30TEP. This field remains valid after SMF30TEP is invalid

SMF30DAS.description: Number of DDs which had their DD Accounting information suppressed

SMF30MRA.description: Adjustment factor for CPU rate. (Number of sixteenths of one CPU microsecond per CPU service unit)

SMF30MRD.description: CPU Time used by dependent enclaves that executed on named system (in hundredths of a second).

SMF30MRI.description: CPU Time used by independent enclaves that executed on named system (in hundredths of a second).

SMF30_MULTISYSTEM_ENCLAVE_REMOTE_SYSTEM_.description: Remote System Data if the address space owns an "original" enclave.

SMF30_NNPICTRS_ENTRY_ID.description: NNPI counter entry identifier, The IFASMFCN macro contains equates and meanings for each entry ID. The equate names start with SMF_NNPICtrs.

SMF30_NNPICTRS_COUNT.description: NNPI Counter value. This field contains the instruction counts used within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step, or job.

SMF30SRV.description: TOTAL SERVICE UNITS This field grows to 'FFFFFFFF'x and then wraps back to zero and continues growing. Once wrapping occurs, SMF30SRV_INV will be set to on. SMF30SRV_L is the 8 byte equivalent of this field.

SMF30CSU.description: CPU SERVICE UNITS This field grows to 'FFFFFFFF'x and then wraps back to zero and continues growing. Once wrapping occurs, SMF30CSU_INV will be set to on. SMF30CSU_L is the 8 byte equivalent of this field.

SMF30SRB.description: SRB SERVICE UNITS This field grows to 'FFFFFFFF'x and then wraps back to zero and continues growing. Once wrapping occurs, SMF30SRB_INV will be set to on. SMF30SRB_L is the 8 byte equivalent of this field.

SMF30IO.description: I/O SERVICE UNITS This field grows to 'FFFFFFFF'x and then wraps back to zero and continues growing. Once wrapping occurs, SMF30IO_INV will be set to on. SMF30IO_L is the 8 byte equivalent of this field.

SMF30MSO.description: MSO SERVICE UNITS This field grows to 'FFFFFFFF'x and then wraps back to zero and continues growing. Once wrapping occurs, SMF30MSO_INV will be set to on. SMF30MSO_L is the 8 byte equivalent of this field.

SMF30SUS.description: Copy of RmctAdjc when this SMF record was produced, measures the number of sixteenths of one microsecond of CPU time per CPU service unit. Note: The value in this field will change when a processor capacity change occurs

SMF30WLM.description: Workload Name - Blanks if the system is operating in workload management compatibility mode.

SMF30SCN.description: Service Class Name - Blanks if the system is operating in workload management compatibility mode.

SMF30GRN.description: Resource Group Name - Blanks if the system is operating in workload management compatibility mode.

SMF30RCN.description: Reporting Class Name - Blanks if the system is operating in workload management compatibility mode.

SMF30ESU.description: Independent Enclave CPU Service Units This field grows to 'FFFFFFFF' and then wraps back to zero and continues growing. Once wrapping occurs, SMF30ESU_INV will be set to on. SMF30ESU_L is the 8 byte equivalent of this field.

SMF30JQT.description: JCL conversion time for batch jobs, 0 for other types of work. 1.024 millisecond units

SMF30RQT.description: Resource and/or system affinity hold time for batch jobs, 0 for other types of work. 1.024 millisecond units

SMF30HQT.description: Hold time not due to system affinity, resource affinity, TYPRUN=HOLD or TYPRUN=JCLHOLD for batch jobs, 0 for other types of work. 1.024 millisecond units

SMF30SQT.description: Time that job was eligible for execution: not held, waiting for an initiator. Valid for all types of work. 1.024 millisecond units

SMF30PFJ.description: Job service class association was modified by a system operator prior to job initiation

SMF30PFR.description: Job service class association was modified by a system operator during job execution

SMF30PFF.description: Job initiation forced by system operator

SMF30WMI.description: Job is executing in a workload manager batch initiator

SMF30CCP.description: Service class assigned was designated CPU-critical

SMF30CSP.description: Service class served was designated storage-critical

SMF30SME.description: Address space cannot be managed to trxn goals

SMF30PIN.description: The following fields contain incomplete data: (SRM could not deliver deltas or values for this interval) SMF30CSU SMF30MSO SMF30SPR SMF30ESU SMF30PFL SMF30SQT SMF30ETA SMF30PFR SMF30SRB SMF30ETC SMF30RCN SMF30SRV SMF30GRN SMF30RES SMF30SUS SMF30HQT SMF30RQT SMF30TAT SMF30IO SMF30RTR SMF30TRS SMF30JPN SMF30SCN SMF30WLM SMF30JQT SMF30SME SMF30CRM SMF30SRV_L SMF30CSU_L SMF30SRB_L SMF30IO_L SMF30MSO_L SMF30ESU_L

SMF30CRM.description: The address space matched a classification rule which specified "manage region using goals of both", which means it is managed towards the velocity goal of the region. But, transaction completions are reported and used for management of the transaction service classes with response time goals. This option should only be used with CICS TORs, the associated AORs should remain at the default "manage region using goals of transaction". */

SMF30SRV_INV.description: Bit 0 When on, indicates that the value in SMF30SRV has grown past its 4 byte maximum value capacity of 'FFFFFFFF'x and has wrapped back to zero. SMF30SRV_L is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30SRV.

SMF30CSU_INV.description: Bit 1 When on, indicates that the value in SMF30CSU has grown past its 4 byte maximum value capacity of 'FFFFFFFF'x and has wrapped back to zero. SMF30CSU_L is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30CSU.

SMF30SRB_INV.description: Bit 2 When on, indicates that the value in SMF30SRB has grown past its 4 byte maximum value capacity of 'FFFFFFFF'x and has wrapped back to zero. SMF30SRB_L is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30SRB.

SMF30IO_INV.description: Bit 3 When on, indicates that the value in SMF30IO has grown past its 4 byte maximum value capacity of 'FFFFFFFF'x and has wrapped back to zero. SMF30IO_L is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30IO.

SMF30MSO_INV.description: Bit 4 When on, indicates that the value in SMF30MSO has grown past its 4 byte maximum value capacity of 'FFFFFFFF'x and has wrapped back to zero. SMF30MSO_L is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30MSO.

SMF30ESU_INV.description: Bit 5 When on, indicates that the value in SMF30ESU has grown past its 4 byte maximum value capacity of 'FFFFFFFF'x and has wrapped back to zero. SMF30ESU_L is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30ESU.

SMF30ZEP.description: Contains information associated with a potential future function, no further details are available at this time

SMF30JPN.description: Subsystem collection name from IWMCLSFY SUBCOLN

SMF30ZNF.description: zAAP Normalization Factor for zAAP service time. Used to convert between real zAAP times and normalized zAAP times, that is, the equivalent time on a standard CP. Multiply SMF30_TIME_ON_zAAP by this value and divide by 256 to calculate the normalized zAAP time.

SMF30SNF.description: zIIP Normalization Factor for zIIP service time. Used to convert between real zIIP times and normalized zIIP times, that is, the equivalent time on a standard CP. Multiply SMF30_TIME_ON_zIIP by this value and divide by 256 to calculate the normalized zIIP time.

SMF30SRV_L.description: TOTAL SERVICE UNITS This is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30SRV. Its value continues to grow after SMF30SRV_INV is set.

SMF30CSU_L.description: CPU SERVICE UNITS This is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30CSU. Its value continues to grow after SMF30CSU_INV is set.

SMF30SRB_L.description: SRB SERVICE UNITS This is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30SRB. Its value continues to grow after SMF30SRB_INV is set.

SMF30IO_L.description: I/O SERVICE UNITS This is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30IO. Its value continues to grow after SMF30IO_INV is set.

SMF30MSO_L.description: MSO SERVICE UNITS This is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30MSO. Its value continues to grow after SMF30MSO_INV is set.

SMF30ESU_L.description: Independent Enclave CPU Service Units This is the 8 byte equivalent of SMF30ESU. Its value continues to grow after SMF30ESU_INV is set.

SMF30ACB.description: Contains information associated with a potential future function, no further details are available at this time

SMF30LGA.description: Contains information associated with a potential future function, no further details are available at this time

SMF30P1A.description: Contains information associated with a potential future function, no further details are available at this time

SMF30CR.description: Contains information associated with a potential future function, no further details are available at this time

SMF30_CAPACITY_CHANGE_CNT.description: The number of processor capacity changes that occurred since the previous interval or event interval. This number will be greater than 1 when the number of processor capacity changes exceeded the number specified in the MAXEVENTINTRECS parmlib option.

SMF30_RCTPCPUA_ACTUAL.description: Physical CPU adjustment factor (i.e. adjustment factor for converting CPU time to equivalent service in basic mode with all processors online). Based on Model Capacity Rating.

SMF30_RCTPCPUA_NOMINAL.description: Physical CPU adjustment factor for collecting CPU time to equivalent service in basic-mode with all processors online). Based on Model Capacity Rating.

SMF30_RCTPCPUA_SCALING_FACTOR.description: Scaling factor for SMF30_RCTPCPUA_Actual and SMF30_RCTPCPUA_Nominal.

SMF30_CAPACITY_ADJUSTMENT_IND.description: When zero, indication is not reported. When in the range 1-99, some amount of reduction is indicated. When 100, the machine is operating at its normal capacity. Primary CPUs and all secondary-type CPUs are similarly affected.

SMF30_CAPACITY_CHANGE_RSN.description: Indicates the reason which is associated with the present value contained in SMF30_Capacity_Adjustment_Ind. The bit values of this field correspond to those described in RMCTZ_Capacity_Adjustment_I ndication of the IRARMCTZ mapping macro (see Data Areas).

SMF30_EVENT_DRIVEN_INTVL_REC.description: When on, indicates that the current interval record was generated as a result of an event, rather than as a result of standard interval expiration based on time.

SMF30_RQSVSUS_ERR.description: When on, indicates that an error occurred while collecting the data for SMF30SUS following a change in processor capacity. If this bit is found to be on when the record is being written, an additional attempt to collect the data from SRM is made. If that attempt is successful, the data is filled in at that time and the SMF30PIN error bit will be off.

SMF30_CAPACITY_DATA_ERR.description: When on, indicates that error occurred while collecting the processor capacity data, therefore the following fields are unreliable: SMF30_RCTPCPUA_Actual SMF30_RCTPCPUA_Nominal SMF30_RCTPCPUA_scaling_factor SMF30_Capacity_Adjustment_Ind SMF30_Capacity_Change_Rsn

SMF30_PCD_RSVD_EXISTS.description: This bit is set in records generated on systems running z/OS 1.7 through z/OS 1.9. It will remain off in records generated at systems running z/OS 1.10 and above.

SMF30CPT.description: STEP CPU TIME UNDER TCB (INCLUDING ENCLAVE TIME). Note that time on zAAP and zIIP is not included. SMF30CPT only includes the consumption of standard CPs, not those of zAAPs and/or zIIPs

SMF30DMI.description: Number of pages moved with ADMF WRITE operation

SMF30DMO.description: Number of pages moved with ADMF READ operation

SMF30ASR.description: Additional CPU time, in hundredths of a second, accumulated by the Preemptable SRB's and Client SRB's for this job. This value is also contained within the value in SMF30CPT.

SMF30ENC.description: Independent enclave CPU time for the step (or job) in hundredths of a second. This value is also contained within the value in SMF30CPT. Note that time on zAAP and zIIP is not included.

SMF30DET.description: Dependent enclave CPU time for the step (or job) in hundredths of a second. This value is also contained within the value in SMF30CPT. Note that time on zAAP and zIIP is not included.

SMF30CEP.description: CPU time consumed for an A/S or Job while enqueue promoted. 1.024 milliseconds unit Unlike SMF30CEPI, this field is "cumulative" even for interval records.

SMF30TF2.description: More failure bits. Each flag name is of form xxxx_F and indicates that field xxxx is not valid

SMF30T32.description: More failure bits. Each flag name is of form xxxx_F and indicates that field xxxx is not valid

SMF30T33.description: More failure bits. Each flag name is of form xxxx_F and indicates that field xxxx is not valid

SMF30_ZIIPBOOST_ACTIVE.description: zIIP boost was active at some point within the interval

SMF30_SPEEDBOOST_ACTIVE.description: Speed boost was active at some point within the interval

SMF30_BOOSTCLASS.description: See SMF30_BoostClass_xxx equates. For step and job records, the boost class when a boost was first found active for the step/job

SMF30_TIME_ON_IFA.description: Time spent on IFA In hundredths of a second (including enclave time)

SMF30_ENCLAVE_TIME_ON_IFA.description: Enclave time spent on IFA In hundredths of a second

SMF30_DEP_ENCLAVE_TIME_ON_IFA.description: Dependent enclave time spent on IFA. In hundredths of a second

SMF30_TIME_IFA_ON_CP.description: IFA CPU time spent on CP In hundredths of a second (including enclave time)

SMF30_ENCLAVE_TIME_IFA_ON_CP.description: IFA Enclave time spent on CP In hundredths of a second

SMF30_DEP_ENCLAVE_TIME_IFA_ON_CP.description: IFA Dependent enclave time spent on CP. In hundredths of a second

SMF30CEPI.description: CPU time consumed for an A/S or Job while enqueue promoted. 1.024 milliseconds unit Unlike SMF30CEP, for interval records, this field contains only the time consumed during the interval itself.

SMF30_TIME_ON_ZIIP.description: Time spent on zIIP In hundredths of a second (including enclave time)

SMF30_ENCLAVE_TIME_ON_ZIIP.description: Enclave time spent on zIIP In hundredths of a second

SMF30_DEPENC_TIME_ON_ZIIP.description: Dependent enclave time spent on zIIP. In hundredths of a second

SMF30_TIME_ZIIP_ON_CP.description: zIIP CPU time spent on CP. When zAAPzIIP=YES is in effect, zAAP-eligible work is included in zIIP CPU time spent on CP. In hundredths of a second (including enclave time)

SMF30_ENCLAVE_TIME_ZIIP_ON_CP.description: zIIP Enclave time spent on CP. When zAAPzIIP=YES is in effect, zAAP-eligible work is included in zIIP Enclave time spent on CP. In hundredths of a second

SMF30_DEPENC_TIME_ZIIP_ON_CP.description: zIIP Dependent enclave time spent on CP. When zAAPzIIP=YES is in effect, zAAP-eligible work is included in zIIP Dependent enclave time spent on CP. In hundredths of a second

SMF30_ENCLAVE_TIME_ZIIP_QUAL.description: Enclave time qualified to run on zIIP. In hundredths of a second

SMF30_DEPENC_TIME_ZIIP_QUAL.description: Dependent enclave time qualified to run on zIIP. In hundredths of a second

SMF30CRP.description: CPU time consumed for an address space or job while promoted due to chronic resource contention (in 1024 millisecond units). For interval records, this field contains only the time consumed during the interval itself.

SMF30ICU_STEP_TERM.description: CPU TCB time spent by the Initiator during job step termination processing. This is the step termination portion of SMF30ICU which is reported in the next step end record

SMF30ICU_STEP_INIT.description: CPU TCB time spent by the Initiator during job step initialization processing. This is the step initialization portion of SMF30ICU for this step end record.

SMF30ISB_STEP_TERM.description: CPU SRB time spent by the Initiator during job step termination processing. This is the step termination portion of SMF30ISB which is reported in the next step end record

SMF30ISB_STEP_INIT.description: CPU SRB time spent by the Initiator during job step initialization processing. This is the step initialization portion of SMF30ISB for this step end record.

SMF30_MISSED_SMF30BLK.description: Accumulated value of I/O block counts when serialization could not be obtained for accumulating the value to SMF30BLK. This value is maintained at the job step level as opposed to the DD level of its SMF30BLK counterpart. This field contains zero for started tasks.

SMF30_MISSED_SMF30DCT.description: Accumulated value of device connect time when serialization could not be obtained for accumulating the value to SMF30DCT. This value is maintained at the job step level as opposed to the DD level of its SMF30DCT counterpart. This field contains zero for started tasks.

SMF30_HIGHEST_TASK_CPU_PERCENT.description: For interval records, the largest percentage of CPU time used by any task in this address space, rounded to the nearest integer. The percentage value is calculated as: TCB time * 100 / interval time. For step-end and job-end records, the value is the largest reported interval value.

SMF30_HIGHEST_TASK_CPU_PROGRAM.description: Program name running in the task that used the largest percentage of CPU time in the address space. This field corresponds to SMF3 0_Highest_Task_CPU_Percent. A value of blanks indicates that no task reported any CPU time in the address space, or that the CPU time could not be obtained. A value of '????????' indicates that the program name could not be obtained for the task that reported the highest percentage of CPU time.

SMF30CAS_INELIGHONORPRIORITY.description: When on, eligible work in this address space is not be offloaded to CPs for help processing. Once this bit is set on for a job interval or step-end record, this bit will also be set on for step-total and job-end records.

SMF30CAS_OA54589.description: Contains data introduced by APAR OA54589

SMF30_TIME_JAVA_ON_ZIIP.description: Time spent in Java work on zIIP in hundredths of a second including enclave time. Valid when SMF30_Time_Java_On_zIIP_F is 0 and SMF30CLN >= SMF30CAS_Len_V2.

SMF30_ENCLAVE_TIME_JAVA_ON_ZIIP.description: Enclave time spent in Java work on zIIP in hundredths of a second. Valid when SMF30_ENCLA VE_Time_Java_On_zIIP_F is 0 and SMF30CLN >= SMF30CAS_Len_V2.

SMF30_DEPENC_TIME_JAVA_ON_ZIIP.description: Dependent enclave time spent in Java work on zIIP in hundredths of a second. Valid when SMF30_DEP ENC_Time_Java_On_zIIP_F is 0 and SMF30CLN >= SMF30CAS_Len_V2.

SMF30_TIME_JAVA_ON_CP.description: zIIP eligible time spent in Java work on CP in hundredths of a second including enclave time. Valid when SMF30_Time_Java_On_CP_F is 0 and SMF30CLN >= SMF30CAS_Len_V2.

SMF30_ENCLAVE_TIME_JAVA_ON_CP.description: zIIP eligible time spent in Java work on CP in hundredths of a second. Valid when SMF30_ENCLA VE_Time_Java_On_CP_F is 0 and SMF30CLN >= SMF30CAS_Len_V2.

SMF30_DEPENC_TIME_JAVA_ON_CP.description: zIIP eligible dependent enclave time spent in Java work on CP in hundredths of a second. Valid when SMF30_DEPENC_Time_Java_On_CP_F is 0 and SMF30CLN >= SMF30CAS_Len_V2.

SMF30SIN.description: The following fields contain incomplete data: (SRM could not deliver deltas or values for this interval) SMF30ERS SMF30KIE SMF30POA SMF30BIA SMF30KOA SMF30POE SMF30BIE SMF30KOE SMF30PSC SMF30BOA SMF30LPI SMF30PSF SMF30BOE SMF30NSW SMF30PSO SMF30CPI SMF30PAI SMF30PST SMF30CPM SMF30PEI SMF30VPI SMF30HPI SMF30PIA SMF30VPO SMF30HPO SMF30PIE SMF30VPR SMF30KIA

SMF30NHU.description: When on, indicates that the NOHONORIEFUSIREGION (no honor IEFUSI region settings) was set in the Program Properties Table (PPT). Region and MEMLIMIT values and limits set or affected by the IEFUSI exit are not honored when this bit is on.

SMF30_RSVDHBB77B0_EXISTS.description: When on the following fields are not valid: SMF30TIH SMF30TIU SMF30TIS These fields are populated at zOS24 and above.

SMF30PGI.description: Number of page ins from auxiliary storage, regardless of the page size (4K or 1M).

SMF30PGO.description: Number of page outs to auxiliary storage, regardless of the page size (4K or 1M).

SMF30NSW.description: As of z/OS 1.8, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.8, this field contained: Number of address space swap sequences. (A swap sequence consists of an address space swap-out and swap-in. Logical swap-out and swap-in are not included.)

SMF30PSI.description: As of z/OS 1.8, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.8, this field contained: Number of pages swapped in from auxiliary storage to central storage. This field includes: (local system queue area (LSQA), fixed pages, and pages that the real storage manager determined to be active when the address space was swapping in. It does not include page reclaims or pages found in storage during the swap-in process (such as pages brought in by the service request blocks (SRB), started after completion of swap-in Stage 1 processing).

SMF30PSO.description: As of z/OS 1.8, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.8, this field contained: Number of pages swapped out from central storage to auxiliary storage. This field includes: local system queue area (LSQA), private area fixed pages, and private area non-fixed changed pages.

SMF30PST.description: As of z/OS 1.8, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.8, this field contained: Number of pages stolen from this address space.

SMF30PSC.description: Number of CPU page milliseconds for this address space. A page millisecond unit equals 1.024 milliseconds * 1 page (4K). It can be used to illustrate the duration of memory consumption where a small spike in memory demand may have less of an impact than a smaller amount of memory used over a longer period of time.

SMF30RGB.description: Maximum possible below 16MB region size, in bytes.

SMF30ERG.description: Maximum possible above 16MB region size, in bytes.

SMF30ARB.description: MAX VIRTUAL SPACE ALLOCATED FROM LSQA AND SWA BELOW 16M

SMF30EAR.description: MAX VIRTUAL SPACE ALLOCATED FROM LSQA AND SWA ABOVE 16M

SMF30URB.description: MAX VIRTUAL SPACE ALLOCATED FROM THE USER REGION BELOW 16M

SMF30EUR.description: MAX VIRTUAL SPACE ALLOCATED FROM THE USER REGION ABOVE 16M

SMF30DSV.description: AMOUNT OF USER KEY DATA SPACE STORAGE (HIGH WATER MARK) USED DURING THE STEP/JOB (IN MEGABYTES)

SMF30PIE.description: As of z/OS 1.6, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.6, this field contained: Number of unblocked pages that were paged in from expanded storage.

SMF30POE.description: As of z/OS 1.6, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.6, this field contained: Number of unblocked pages that were paged out to expanded storage.

SMF30BIA.description: NUMBER OF BLOCKED PAGES PAGED IN FROM AUXILIARY STORAGE

SMF30BOA.description: NUMBER OF BLOCKED PAGES PAGED OUT TO AUXILIARY STORAGE

SMF30BIE.description: As of z/OS 1.6, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.6, this field contained: Number of blocked pages that were paged in from expanded storage.

SMF30BOE.description: As of z/OS 1.6, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.6, this field contained: Number of blocked pages that were paged out to expanded storage.

SMF30KIA.description: NUMBER OF BLOCKS PAGED IN FROM AUXILIARY STORAGE

SMF30KOA.description: NUMBER OF BLOCKS PAGED OUT TO AUXILIARY STORAGE

SMF30KIE.description: As of z/OS 1.6, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.6, this field contained: Number of blocks that were paged in from expanded storage.

SMF30KOE.description: As of z/OS 1.6, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.6, this field contained: Number of blocks that were paged out to expanded storage.

SMF30PSF.description: Number of CPU page seconds for the shared central storage frames in use by this address space, in page millisecond units

SMF30PAI.description: Number of shared pages that were paged in from auxiliary storage in this address space

SMF30PEI.description: As of z/OS 1.6, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.6, this field contained: Number of IARVSERV shared pages that were paged in from expanded storage in this address space.

SMF30ERS.description: As of z/OS 1.6, this field is no longer valid. This value will always be zero. Prior to z/OS 1.6, this field contained: Expanded storage page residency time in page-milliseconds

SMF30MEM.description: MEMLIMIT value in 1MB units as determined at step initialization time, after IEFUSI and SMFLIMxx processing. Changes to the MEMLIMIT value after step initialization time are not reflected here. Refer to the related documentation to see how the MEMLIMIT value can change. The maximum value of this field is '00000FFFFFFFF000'x that is equivalent to MEMLIMIT having no limit.

SMF30SLM.description: Actions taken on the job step region or memlimit due to a rule coded in the SMFLIMxx parmlib member. For subtype 5, this will be a copy of the last executed step's SMF30SLM value

SMF30SL1.description: When on, SMFLIM REGIONBELOW acted on the non-extended REGION for this step

SMF30SL2.description: When on, SMFLIM REGIONABOVE acted on the extended REGION for this step

SMF30SL3.description: When on, SMFLIM SYSRESVBELOW acted on the non-extended REGION for this step

SMF30SL4.description: When on, SMFLIM SYSRESVABOVE acted on the extended REGION for this step

SMF30SL5.description: When on, SMFLIM MEMLIMIT acted on the MEMLIMIT for this step

SMF30SL6.description: When on, the IEFUSI exit set the output flag that caused all SMFLIM decision making to be bypassed

SMF30_USERKEYCOMMONAUDITENABLED.description: When on, successful and unsuccessful user key common storage usage attempts is enabled for this step. SMF30_USERKEYCSAUSAGE, SMF30_USERKEYCADSUSAGE, SMF30_USERKEYCHANGKEYUSAGE, SMF30_USERKEYRUCSAUSAGE and SMF30_RUCSAEarlyUsage are only applicable when this flag is on.

SMF30_USERKEYCSAUSAGE.description: When on, successful or unsuccessful attempts were made to obtain user key CSA or RUCSA storage for this step. See SMF30_USERKEYRUCSAUSAGE for RUCSA specific usage. This bit is only valid when SMF30_U serKeyCommonAuditEnabled is on. Once this bit is on within a step, it will stay on for the step. The bit will be on in job end records if the bit is on for any step in the job.

SMF30_USERKEYCADSUSAGE.description: When on, successful or unsuccessful attempts were made to create a user key CADS for this step. This bit is only valid when SMF30_UserKeyC ommonAuditEnabled is on. Once this bit is on within a step, it will stay on for the step. The bit will be on in job end records if the bit is on for any step in the job.

SMF30_USERKEYCHANGKEYUSAGE.description: When on, successful or unsuccessful attempts were made to change the key of common ESQA storage to a user key (via CHANGKEY) for this step. This bit is only valid when SMF30_UserKeyC ommonAuditEnabled is on. Once this bit is on within a step, it will stay on for the step. The bit will be on in job end records if the bit is on for any step in the job.

SMF30_USERKEYRUCSAUSAGE.description: When on, successful or unsuccessful attempts were made to obtain, reference or free user key RUCSA storage for this step Once this bit is on within a step, it will stay on for the step. The bit will be on in job end records if the bit is on for any step in the job.

SMF30_RUCSAEARLYUSAGE.description: When on, successful access to RUCSA was made by an address space that was authorized to RUCSA during early IPL or early started task initialization due to DIAGxx VSM AllowEarlyRucsa(YES) Scope is life of an address space

SMF30HVR.description: High water mark for the number of real storage frames that is used to back 64-bit private storage. The high water mark does not include 2G frames.

SMF30HVA.description: High water mark for the number of auxiliary storage slots used to back 64-bit private storage

SMF30HVO.description: Amount of 64-bit private storage in bytes obtained by this step/job. This includes guarded virtual storage

SMF30HVH.description: High water mark for the number of usable bytes of 64-bit private storage that is obtained by this step or job. This does not include guarded virtual storage. Note: this is not the amount of 64-bit High Virtual storage that is charged toward the MEMLIMIT as it includes IARV64 MEMLIMIT=NO storage as well.

SMF30HSO.description: Amount of 64-bit shared storage in bytes this step/job has addressability or access to

SMF30HSH.description: High water mark for the number of usable bytes of 64-bit IARV64 REQUEST=SHAREMEMOBJ shared storage to which this step or job has access. This does not include guard areas which are, by definition, not usable.

SMF30TIH.description: High water mark of TIOT space used for TIOT entries (in bytes.)

SMF30TIU.description: Current TIOT space used for TIOT entries (in bytes.) This will only contain a non-zero value for interval records, since TIOT entries are freed by unallocation processing at step end and job end.

SMF30TIS.description: Size of TIOT available for TIOT entries (in bytes.) This does not include the space reserved by the system for the TIOT Prefix, Header, and Trailer.

SMF30NUMBEROFDATASPACESHWM.description: The high water mark of the number of data spaces owned by this job step.

SMF30USERDATASPACECREATEREQCOUNT.description: The number of requests to create data spaces during this job step.

SMF30_DMEMREQUESTED2G.description: Requested Dedicated Memory in 2G units at start of job step

SMF30_DMEMMINREQUESTED2G.description: Requested minimum amount of Dedicated Memory in 2G units at start of job step

SMF30_DMEMASSIGNED2G.description: Assigned Dedicated Memory in 2G units at start of job step

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEAS2G.description: Number of 2G Dedicated Memory frames in use

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEASFIXED1M.description: Number of fixed 1M Dedicated Memory frames in use

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEASPAGEABLE1M.description: Number of pageable 1M Dedicated Memory frames in use

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEAS4K.description: Number of 4K Dedicated Memory frames in use

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEASDATTABLES.description: Number of 4K Dedicated Memory frames in use as DAT tables

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEAS4KHWM.description: High water mark for the number of Dedicated real storage frames (4K units) that is used to back 64-bit private storage

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEASPAGEABLE1MHWM.description: High water mark for the number of Dedicated real storage frames (1M units) that is used to back pageable 1M pages

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEASFIXED1MHWM.description: High water mark for the number of Dedicated real storage frames (1M units) that is used to back fixed 1M pages

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEAS2GHWM.description: High water mark for the number of Dedicated real storage frames (2G units) that is used to back 2G pages

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEASDATTABLESHWM.description: High water mark for the number of Dedicated real storage frames (4K units) that is used to back DAT tables

SMF30_DMEMNUMINUSEHWM.description: High water mark for the number of Dedicated Memory frames in use 4K units

SMF30_DMEMNUM2GFAILED.description: Count of requested 2G frames eligible to be backed by Dedicated Memory frames but were not due to availability

SMF30_DMEMNUM1MFAILED.description: Count of requested 1M frames eligible to be backed by Dedicated Memory frames but were not due to availability

SMF30_DMEMNUM4KFAILED.description: Count of requested 4K frames eligible to be backed by Dedicated Memory frames but were not due to availability

SMF30_NUMINUSEAS2GHWM.description: Number of 2G frames in use by job step high water mark

SMF30_NUM2GFAILED.description: Number of 2G frames that could not be obtained because none were available at the time of the IARV64 request

SMF30_OBTAINSHOMESPACE.description: Number of GETMAIN or STORAGE OBTAIN requests within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step or job. Results are for the home address space at the time of the invocation.

SMF30_IARV64OBTAINSHOMESPACE.description: Number of IARV64 GETSTOR and GETCOMMON requests within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step or job. Results are for the home address space at the time of the invocation.

SMF30_FRAMESFIRSTREFERENCEBACKING.description: Count of real storage frames (4K units) backing both 31-bit and 64-bit virtual storage within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step or job. Count includes dedicated real storage frames.

SMF30_SUMREAL1M.description: Sum of samples of the amount of real memory (includes Dedicated Memory) in 1M units within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step or job.

SMF30_SUMSQUARESREAL1M.description: Sum of squared samples of the amount of real memory (includes Dedicated Memory) in 1M units within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step or job.

SMF30_NUMSAMPLES.description: Number of samples for both SMF30_SumReal1M and SMF30_SumSquaresReal1M within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step or job.

SMF30_HWMHVREAL1M.description: High water mark for the number, in 1M units, of real frames (includes Dedicated Memory) backing 64-bit virtual private storage for all frame types (4K, 1M and 2G) within the scope of the record, either for the current interval, job step or job.

SMF30_CRYPCTRS_ACTIVE.description: Indicates that crypto counter processing is active

SMF30_NNPICTRS_ACTIVE.description: Indicates that NNPI counter processing is active

SMF70BNP.description: Number of physical processors assigned for PR/SM use

SMF70NPC.description: PR/SM - Number of physical processors has changed

SMF70TSC.description: PR/SM - Dispatch interval value has changed

SMF70PHY.description: PR/SM - An additional partition is presented with the name "PHYSICAL". This partition includes all of the otherwise uncaptured time which was used by LPAR but could not be attributed to a specific logical partition

SMF70DGE.description: PR/SM - Diagnose X'204' extended data is supported

SMF70VMG.description: Simplified Diagnose X'204' data provided for system running as z/VM guest. CPU consumption by z/VM itself provided with partition data section named "PHYSICAL"

SMF70WUC.description: Service units available to MVS image changed

SMF70RCU.description: SMF70LAC is provided for systems running in LPAR mode, as a z/VM guest, or under an alternate virtual machine. The value does no longer include CPU wait times.

SMF70HWV.description: SMF70MDL is the model-capacity identifier and SMF70HWM is the physical model. If OFF, SMF70MDL represents both model-capacity identifier and physical model

SMF70PTC.description: CP promote slices (OPT parameter BLWLTRPCT) changed

SMF70PLC.description: Swapped-in starvation threshold (OPT parameter BLWLINTHD) changed

SMF70GTS.description: PR/SM - Dispatch accumulated interval time in milliseconds. A zero value indicates that the dispatch interval was dynamically determined

SMF70MDL.description: EBCDIC CPC model identifier. See Bit 4 of SMF70STF (SMF70HWV)

SMF70IFA.description: zAAPs online at the end of the interval

SMF70WLA.description: Millions of service units available to MVS image when not running as VM guest. If running as VM guest, capactity available to VM

SMF70LAC.description: Long-term average CPU service in millions of service units. For details, see RCTLACS of IRARCT. Scope of value depends on Bit 3 of SMF70STF (SMF70RCU).

SMF70HOF.description: Hypervisor date/time offset (aka Sysplex timer offset)

SMF70HWM.description: EBCDIC CPC physical model identifier. Valid if Bit 4 of SMF70STF (SMF70HWV) is set.

SMF70SUP.description: zIIPs online at the end of the interval

SMF70GJT.description: Time when the partition that wrote this record has joined or left its capacity group (last change of group name). Also set at IPL time when no member of a capacity group.

SMF70POM.description: EBCDIC plant code that identifies the plant of manufacture for the configuration. The plant code is left-justified with trailing blank characters if necessary

SMF70CSC.description: EBCDIC sequence code of the configuration. The sequence code is right-justified with leading EBCDIC zeroes if necessary

SMF70HIF.description: Failure returned by HisMT service. Values in logical core data section, multithreading capacity factors and average thread density values are invalid.

SMF70PMI.description: Accumulated number of blocked dispatachable units per second that may get promoted in their dispatch priority. To get the average promote event rate, divide SMF70PMI by SMF70SAM

SMF70PMU.description: Number of blocked dispatchable units being promoted during the interval

SMF70PMW.description: Accumulated number of address spaces and enclaves being blocked during the interval. To get the average number of waiters for promote, divide SMF70PMW by SMF70SAM.

SMF70PMP.description: Maximum number of address spaces and enclaves found being blocked during the interval

SMF70PMT.description: 1/1000s of the CPU capacity for promote slices (OPT parameter BLWLTRPCT)

SMF70PML.description: Swapped-in starvation threshold. When an address space or enclave not received CPU service within this time interval although it has ready-to-tun work, it is considered being blocked (OPT parameter BLWLINTHD)

SMF70MPC.description: When non-zero, EBCDIC model permanent capacity identifier of the configuration. The identifier is left justified with trailing blanks if necessary.

SMF70MTC.description: When non-zero, EBCDIC model temporary capacity identifier of the configuration. The identifier is left justified with trailing blanks if necessary.

SMF70MCR.description: Model capacity rating. When non-zero, this value is associated with the model capacity as identified in field SMF70MDL.

SMF70MPR.description: Model permanent capacity rating. When non-zero, this value is associated with the model capacity as identified in field SMF70MPC.

SMF70MTR.description: Model temporary capacity rating. When non-zero, this value is associated with the model capacity as identified in field SMF70MTC.

SMF70NRM.description: Normalization factor for zIIP Multiply zIIP time by this value and divide by 256 to get the equivalent time on a CP

SMF70GAU.description: Long-term average of CPU service in millions of service units which would be allowed by the limit of the capacity group but is not used by its members. If the value is negative, this capacity group is capped. Valid if Bit 7 of SMF70STF (SMF70GAV) set.

SMF70NCR.description: Nominal model-capacity rating. When non-zero, this value is associated with the nominal model capacity as identified in field SMF70MDL. When field SMF70CAI contains a value of 100, this value equals the value in field SMF70MCR.

SMF70NPR.description: Nominal permanent model-capacity rating. When non-zero, this value is associated with the nominal permanent model capacity as identified in field SMF70MPC. When field SMF70CAI contains a value of 100, this value equals the value in field SMF70MPR.

SMF70NTR.description: Nominal temporary model-capacity rating. When non-zero, this value is associated with the nominal temporary model capacity as identified in field SMF70MTC. When field SMF70CAI contains a value of 100, this value equals the value in field SMF70MTR.

SMF70CAI.description: Capacity-adjustment indication. When zero, the indication is not reported. When in the range 1 to 99, some amount of reduction is indicated. When 100, the machine is operating at its normal capacity. Temporary capacity changes that affect machine performance (for example, CBU or OOCoD) are not included

SMF70CCR.description: Capacity-change reason. Valid if SMF70CAI is non-zero. When 1, the capacity change is due to the setting of a manual control. When greater than 1, capacity change is due to an internal machine condition

SMF70MCP.description: Maximum CPU address available at this IPL

SMF70ICP.description: Highest CPU Id installed at IPL time

SMF70CCP.description: Highest CPU Id currently installed This number can increase upon dynamic CPU addition

SMF70CPA_ACTUAL.description: Physical CPU adjustment factor based on Model Capacity Rating (will be used for converting processor time to service units). This value together with SMF70CPUA_scaling_factor replaces SMF70CPA.

SMF70MCF.description: Multithreading maximum capacity numerator for general purpose processors. Divide this value by 1024 to get the multithreading maximum capacity factor for all general purpose processors that were configured ONLINE for the complete interval.

SMF70MCFS.description: Multithreading maximum capacity numerator for zIIP processors. Divide this value by 1024 to get the multithreading maximum capacity factor for all zIIPs that were configured ONLINE for the complete interval. A zero value is reported if no zIIP is currently installed

SMF70MCFI.description: Multithreading maximum capacity numerator for zAAP processors. Divide this value by 1024 to get the multithreading maximum capacity factor for all zAAPs that were configured ONLINE for the complete interval. A zero value is reported if no zAAP is currently installed

SMF70CF.description: Multithreading capacity numerator for general purpose processors. Divide this value by 1024 to get the multithreading capacity factor for all general purpose processors that were configured ONLINE for the complete interval.

SMF70CFS.description: Multithreading capacity numerator for zIIP processors. Divide this value by 1024 to get get the multithreading capacity factor for all zIIPs that were configured ONLINE for the complete interval. A zero value is reported if no zIIP is currently installed

SMF70CFI.description: Multithreading capacity numerator for zAAP processors. Divide this value by 1024 to get get the multithreading capacity factor for all zAAPs that were configured ONLINE for the complete interval. A zero value is reported if no zAAP is currently installed

SMF70ATD.description: Average Thread Density numerator for general purpose processors. Divide this value by 1024 to get the average number of active threads for all general purpose processors that were dispatched to physical hardware and configured ONLINE for the complete interval.

SMF70ATDS.description: Average Thread Density numerator for zIIP. Divide this value by 1024 to get the average number of active threads for all zIIPs that were dispatched to physical hardware and configured ONLINE for the complete interval. A zero value is reported if no zIIP is currently installed

SMF70ATDI.description: Average Thread Density numerator for zAAP. Divide this value by 1024 to get the average number of active threads for all zAAPs that were dispatched to physical hardware and configured ONLINE for the complete interval. A zero value is reported if no zAAP is currently installed

SMF70LACM.description: Long-term average CPU service (millions of service units) consumed by transactions classified with reporting attribute MOBILE. If an address space or enclave is part of a tenant resource group, it will not contribute to SMF70LACM.

SMF70LACA.description: Long-term average CPU service (millions of service units) consumed by transactions classified with reporting attribute CATEGORYA. If an address space or enclave is part of a tenant resource group, it will not contribute to SMF70LACA.

SMF70LACB.description: Long-term average CPU service (millions of service units) consumed by transactions classified with reporting attribute CATEGORYB. If an address space or enclave is part of a tenant resource group, it will not contribute to SMF70LACB.

SMF70ADJ.description: Logical adjustment factor for CPU rate

SMF70LACCR.description: Long-term average CPU service (millions of service units) consumed by DFSMS data set encryption. Valid only for IBM z14 and later CPCs

SMF70MAXPU.description: When non-zero, this field indicates how many processor cores are physically available in this particular machine. When the value is 0, it is not defined for this model.

SMF70OS_PRTCT.description: When non-zero, OSPROTECT system parameter with value other than SYSTEM is in effect. X'01' indicates OSPROTECT=1. May be 0 for IBM z15 and later machines when OSPROTECT=1

SMF70_TRG_M_CNT.description: Number of times sampling of tenant resource group memory consumption happened

SMF70MDL_VAR.description: EBCDIC model variable capacity identifier. The identifier is left justified with trailing blanks if necessary. This field is zero, if not supported by the hardware.

SMF70MVCR.description: Model variable capacity rating. When non-zero, this value is associated with the model capacity as identified in field SMF70MDL_VAR.

SMF70NVCR.description: Nominal model variable capacity rating. When non-zero, this value is associated with the nominal model capacity as identified in field SMF70MDL_VAR. When field SMF70CAI contains a value of 100, this value equals the value in field SMF70MVCR.

SMF70ZSU_ON_ZIIP.description: Unweighted zIIP-eligible service units spent on zIIP for the entire system

SMF70ZSU_ON_CP.description: Unweighted zIIP-eligible service units spent on CP for the entire system

SMF70JSU_ON_ZIIP.description: Unweighted zIIP-eligible Java service units spent on zIIP for the entire system

SMF70JSU_ON_CP.description: Unweighted zIIP-eligible Java service units spent on CP for the entire system

SMF70CPE_LO.description: Low threshold value of OPT parameter CPENABLE

SMF70CPE_HI.description: High threshold value of OPT parameter CPENABLE

SMF70MTI.description: CPU is offline while core is online

SMF70DCI.description: Data available for a complete interval

SMF70PAR.description: CPU was varied during Postprocessor duration interval

SMF70VAC.description: Data invalid, CPU reconfigured in measurement interval

SMF70STA.description: CPU online at end of interval

SMF70TYP.description: CPU type: 0 = General purpose CP 1 = zAAP 2 = zIIP

SMF70SLH.description: Num of entries to the I/O SLIH

SMF70VFS.description: Number of samples where the vector bit in the PSA image was ON

SMF70NIO.description: Number of I/Os for this CPU

SMF70SIG.description: Total number of SIGPs done by this CPU

SMF70WTD.description: Wait dispatch count for this CPU

SMF70WTS.description: The number of times PR/SM issued a warning-track interruption to a logical processor and z/OS was able to return the logical processor to PR/SM within the grace period

SMF70WTU.description: The number of times PR/SM issued a warning-track interruption to a logical processor and z/OS was unable to return the logical processor to PR/SM within the grace period

SMF70WTI.description: Amount of time in milliseconds that a logical processor was yielded to PR/SM due to warning track processing

SMF70CTN.description: Number of physical CPUs of this type at interval end

SMF70CAN.description: Accumulated number of physical CPUs. Divide by SMF70DSA to get the average number of physical CPUs of this type applicable during the interval.

SMF70_LPB_VALID.description: Core LPAR Busy time is valid

SMF70_CPU_SKIP.description: The CPU data sections for this core are grouped together in the record. To get to the first CPU data section associated with this logical core, skip over the number of CPU data sections specified by this field, starting at the first CPU data section in the record.

SMF70_CPU_NUM.description: Number of CPU data sections for this core. This value represents the number of threads that are active on this core.

SMF70_PROD.description: Multithreading core productivity numerator. Divide this value by 1024 to get the multithreading core productivity. A zero value is reported if the core was not configured ONLINE for the complete interval. If SMF70_CPU_NUM is greater than 1, the core productivity represents the percentage of how much work the core resources accomplished while dispatched to physical hardware over the maximum amount of work the core resources could have accomplished while dispatched to physical hardware.

SMF70_LPAR_BUSY.description: Multithreading Core LPAR Busy time in milliseconds. This field is valid if bit 0 of SMF70_CORE_FLG is set.

SMF70M3R.description: Record was written by RMF Monitor III

SMF70RCL.description: SMF record converted to lower service level. Bit is set by SMF record retrieval service GRBSMFR.

SMF70RCH.description: SMF record converted to higher release or service level. Bit is set by SMF record retrieval service GRBSMFR.

SMF70ALTVM.description: Running under an alternate virtual machine environment

SMF70IIP.description: zIIP boost was active during entire interval

SMF70EED.description: Speed boost was active during entire interval

SMF70BOO.description: Boost class is set at end of interval, valid only when zIIP boost and/or Speed boost is active: 001 IPL, 010 Shutdown, 011 Recovery Process

SMF70MVS.description: MVS software level (consists of an acronym and the version, release, and modification level - ZVvvrrmm)

SMF70IML.description: Indicates the type of processor complex on which data measurements were taken. X'03' = 9672, zSeries

SMF70PRI.description: At least one zAAP is currently installed

SMF70PRP.description: At least one zIIP is currently installed

SMF70RAO.description: Offset to reassembly area relative to start of RMF product section

SMF70RAL.description: Length of reassembly area. Area consists of a fixed header and a variable number of information blocks. Length depends on the record type/subtype, but is fixed for a specific type/subtype

SMF70RAN.description: Number of reassembly area. This field is used to indicate whether SMF record is broken. If 0, record is not broken. If 1, record is broken. Offset and length are only valid if SMFxxRAN is 1. Reassembly area is only present in broken records.

SMF70OIL.description: Original interval length as defined in the session or by SMF (in seconds)

SMF70GIE.description: Projected gathering interval end GMT time

SMF70XNM.description: Sysplex name as defined in ECVTSPLX

SMF70SNM.description: System name for current system as defined in CVTSNAME

SMF70PDT.description: Logical processor total dispatch time, in microseconds. When associated with partition name *PHYSICAL*, this field contains the accumulated number of microseconds during which a physical CPU was busy but the time could not be attributed to a specific logical partition. This time includes the time PR/SM was controlling the physical processor (LPAR management time) as well as any other time the processor was busy for any reason such as managing coupling facility traffic.

When associated with partition name *PHYSICAL*, this field contains the accumulated number of microseconds during which a physical CPU was busy but the time could not be attributed to a specific logical partition or to LPAR management of the physical processor. One example is time managing coupling facility traffic. This field is zero, if not supported by the hardware. LPAR management time is the time from SMF70PDT associated with partition name *PHYSICAL* less the contents of this field.

The value may be the same or different for all shared CPUs of type SMF70CIX. This is an accumulated value. Divide by the number of Diagnose samples SMF70DSA to get the average weight value for the interval.
